term.def: The computing power needed to train and run AI. When people talk about a compute crisis, they mean AI demand is growing faster than the chips available.

prompt.prompt: Act as a tough client at a [type of company]. I will pitch my plan for [project]. Ask me five hard questions, one at a time, then give me honest feedback on my answers.

quiz.q: The Verge reports that McKinsey is making job applicants spar with a fake AI client.
quiz.why: That is what the headline says. It shows AI is now appearing in how some firms test candidates.

quiz.q: TechCrunch reports that Ricursive Intelligence is betting on AI-designed chips to help solve the compute crisis.
quiz.why: That is what the headline says. Compute means the computing power AI needs, and chips supply it.

quiz.q: If an AI tool sounds confident, its answer must be correct.
quiz.why: AI can write wrong answers in a smooth, sure tone. Always check important facts, numbers and names.

quiz.q: Adding details like your audience, your goal and the format you want to a prompt usually gives a better answer.
quiz.why: AI works with what you give it. Clear context means fewer guesses and less rewriting for you.

quiz.q: Once an AI tool writes a draft, a person no longer needs to check it before it goes out.
quiz.why: AI can make mistakes or miss context. A human should review anything that goes to customers, bosses or the public.
